title: Sacramento Temple Hosts Diwali Annakut With Hundreds of Vegetarian Offerings
excerpt: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Mather opens its Diwali and Hindu New Year celebrations on November 1 with an Annakut display, family carnival and food stalls, ahead of Diwali night on November 8.
body:
• BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Mather hosts its Diwali Annakutotsav on Sunday, November 1, 2026, from 12 p.m. to 5 p.m., with darshan closing at 5:30 p.m.
  • The centerpiece is the Annakut, a grand display of vegetarian dishes offered to God; BAPS says its North American celebrations this year feature hundreds of dishes prepared by devotees.
  • The afternoon also includes Nilkanth Varni Abhishek, an exhibit, rangoli, decorations, food stalls, a carnival and prasad, with registration through Eventbrite.
  • Diwali itself falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, when the mandir holds Chopda Pujan from 6 p.m. to 8 p.m., followed by Hindu New Year darshan on November 10.

SACRAMENTO, Calif. — Families across the Sacramento area are invited to celebrate Diwali and the Hindu New Year at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, where the temple's Diwali Annakutotsav on Sunday, November 1, will center on one of the festival's oldest food traditions: the Annakut, a grand display of vegetarian dishes offered to God. KCRA 3 previewed the celebration as an afternoon of cultural traditions, colorful decorations and food for Sacramento-area families.

Diwali, the Festival of Lights, marks the triumph of light over darkness and good over evil and is one of the most widely celebrated festivals in the Hindu calendar. In Sacramento, where Indian American communities are concentrated in neighborhoods from Elk Grove and Natomas to Folsom, the festival now stretches across several weekends of temple programs, city events and home celebrations. The BAPS mandir, at 10548 Armstrong Avenue in Mather, is the region's largest single Diwali gathering point.

The Annakut Offering

Annakut, literally a mountain of food, is traditionally offered on the day associated with the Hindu New Year, in gratitude for the year past and to seek blessings for the year ahead. Devotees prepare vegetarian dishes at home and in the temple kitchen, then arrange them before the sacred images for darshan, after which the sanctified food is shared as prasad.

BAPS says its Shri Swaminarayan Mandirs across North America marked Diwali and the Hindu New Year this year with Annakut offerings of hundreds of vegetarian dishes, prepared by devotees and supported by volunteers through seva, or selfless service. This year's BAPS theme, "Light Beyond Lamps: Journey Through Hindu Sanskruti," presents Hinduism as a living way of life tied to family, gratitude, service and community, with celebrations also featuring rangoli, illuminated diyas and festive decorations.

An Afternoon Built Around Families

The mandir's own listing for November 1, from 12 p.m. to 5 p.m., emphasizes family harmony. Alongside Annakut darshan, visitors can take part in Nilkanth Varni Abhishek, view an exhibit, and walk grounds decorated with rangoli. Food stalls, a carnival, prasad and gifts are also part of the afternoon, and every visitor receives a New Year calendar. Darshan closes at 5:30 p.m., and the temple asks visitors to register in advance through its Eventbrite page for the event.

For many families in the region, the Annakut afternoon is the public face of a festival otherwise observed at home. A Sacramento Diwali guide notes that the city's celebrations run from Elk Grove's free city festival on October 22 to the mandir programs in Mather, and that neighborhoods with strong Indian communities, including Elk Grove, Natomas and Folsom, light up with diyas through the season.

Diwali Week Continues at the Mandir

Diwali itself falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026. That evening, from 6 p.m. to 8 p.m., the mandir holds Chopda Pujan for adults and Sharda Pujan for children. In the Chopda Pujan ceremony, business owners and families bring conventional account books, ledgers and checkbooks, as well as laptops, tablets and phones, to be blessed for the new financial year. The Sacramento guide puts the Lakshmi Puja muhurat, the auspicious evening window for the festival's central prayer, at 5:19 p.m. to 7:09 p.m. that day.

The observances close on Tuesday, November 10, with Hindu New Year darshan at the mandir. Morning arti darshan begins at 7:15 a.m., and the evening program runs from 6 p.m. to 8 p.m., with Thal singing at 6:30 p.m., evening arti darshan at 7 p.m., and a Sneh Milan gathering with mahaprasad at 7:20 p.m.

If You Go

The Diwali Annakutotsav is on Sunday, November 1, 2026, from 12 p.m. to 5 p.m. at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, 10548 Armstrong Avenue, Mather. Registration is through the temple's Eventbrite page, and darshan closes at 5:30 p.m. First-time visitors do not need to be Hindu to attend; the mandir presents the afternoon as a family event open to the wider Sacramento community.
